reason: The hypothesis proposes applying pack cementation aluminization, a known coating technique, to refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) to form a protective Al2O3 scale. While the individual elements (aluminization, Al2O3 protection) are well-known, no passage applies this specific intervention to RHEAs. P2 and P3 discuss RHEA oxidation and note that a protective Al2O3 layer was hindered by CrTaO4, and P7 explicitly suggests future work on promoting Al2O3. The hypothesis directly addresses this gap by proposing a surface engineering solution, which is a non-trivial transfer of a known technique to a new alloy class with a stated reason.
